name: postcontrast-arms

cpu.note: the speed study's round 1, run pc-s100-today14: 100 stacks in 1,032.3 s, 329.8 CPU seconds a stack, every answer equal to model r1's frozen ones. The arms' own arithmetic is under a millisecond a stack, so this is the rate of the features they read. The served fallback postcontrast-full was timed only with a card for its tools: 0.1498 a second over the 377 stacks stage 1 deferred in the speed sample (pcf-speed, T25's F1, run t25-20261014T000311); no CPU-alone pass of the served package was measured
cpu.hardware: 14 stacks at a time on the CPU alone in the research container (64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB), the archive over NFS 4.2, cold; model r1's own feature code (N4, SynthSeg, SynthStrip, SynthMorph and the Frangi filter from FreeSurfer's image) feeding these arms

limits: Trained on the group's own data: a site model, never exported and never in a release (spec 10.6)
Arithmetic per stack on the CPU; the tools that make their features take a card in postcontrast-full, whose speed is on the cascade's card
The full pipeline's grade against model r1 (its plan's test A) is not on this card until it is graded

params.what: model r1's three frozen image arms (T, U, V) exported to JSON with the HP and VX atlases they were fitted on, inside it byte for byte; the full pipeline (postcontrast-full) computes their features from SynthMorph, SynthSeg and SynthStrip

tested.claim: the arms' JSON against model r1's pickle on every row of model r1's table and round 4's reference tables (P1 of the full pipeline's plan): the same availability and every probability within 1e-12

intended_use: The image arms of model r1 in the post-contrast fallback, postcontrast-full, over the stacks the cascade defers; the cascade names them among its parts (encoder names the student that imitates them, as the engine's kinds have a head read an encoder)
